sources.entry: LLaVA - Large Language and Vision Assistant #opensource

summary.name: LLaVA
summary.one_liner: LLaVA (Large Language and Vision Assistant) is an open-source multimodal model that connects a CLIP vision encoder to the Vicuna language model for visual chat and science question answering.
use_cases: chat about images with an AI assistant
building a vision-language dataset from GPT-4 outputs
summary.what_it_does: LLaVA is an end-to-end trained large multimodal model that pairs a CLIP ViT-L/14 visual encoder with the Vicuna LLM through a simple projection matrix. It is trained in two stages: first feature alignment with only the projection updated on a CC3M subset, then end-to-end fine-tuning for visual chat or Science QA. The authors generated 158K language-image instruction-following samples from COCO images using language-only GPT-4, split into conversation, detailed description, and complex reasoning. They report 85.1% relative score versus GPT-4 on a 90-instruction evaluation set of 30 unseen images, and 92.53% accuracy on Science QA. The data, code, and checkpoints are publicly released.
notable: Instruction data generated by text-only GPT-4 from COCO images (LLaVA-Instruct-150K)
Reports 85.1% relative score vs GPT-4 and 92.53% on Science QA
Public release of data, code, and model checkpoints
caveats: Research use only; the license restricts use to research and follows CLIP, LLaMA, Vicuna and GPT-4 terms
Dataset is CC BY-NC 4.0, so non-commercial use only
Models trained on the dataset should not be used outside research
